findings.issue: The permissions table, which is the full A03.1-A45 change list and the source of oracle invariant 5 ('exactly the M19 cells listed'), has no read cell for several routes. There is no filing read (GET /v1/reporting/filings, /{id}, /{id}/pack), no staff read of grants, their activity or the collections catalogue (GET /v1/dataroom/grants, /{id}/activity, /v1/dataroom/collections), no read of report exports (GET /v1/reports/exports, /{id}) and no obligation-history read. The spec says TP-LIC sees reportable_situation_notice filings and TP-RE sees outside_tmd filings, but no cell grants that. No table maps routes to action ids, so 'permission tests on every endpoint' have no expected result. A build could leave these routes unguarded and still pass, or deny them to everyone and break ADM-26's Filings and Data room tabs and the partner views.
findings.fix: Add M19.filing.read (LEGL, CCO, CFO, CEO; TP-LIC own-records for filings addressed to its licensee entity; TP-RE own-vehicles for outside_tmd; delegable true), M19.dataRoomGrant.read (CCO, SECO, LEGL; grantee own grants), M19.report.read (the requester's own exports plus CFO and CCO) and a history read. Add an endpoint -> action-id table that covers every route in the HTTP API section, including the _test routes (local only). Carry both into the A03.1-A45 change list and oracle invariant 5.

findings.issue: The person-only refusal codes are unreachable and have two sources. M19.filing.submit and M19.metricValue.markAudited are delegable 'counsel', so under A03 section 8 a token can never hold the scope: validateTokenScopes refuses it at issuance with SCOPE_PENDING_COUNSEL, and a call is refused by A12 for the missing scope. The pass criterion that tokens are refused 'with FIL_PERSON_ONLY, MET_ATTEST_PERSON_ONLY' therefore cannot be met as written. The person-only rule is also held both as an A45 set_with_counsel row and as A03's delegable flag. The Agent parity paragraph still lists 'a mark-audited request' among the drafts a token can open, and the sensitive-agent-actions list includes an agent drafting one.
findings.fix: Make A03's delegable flag the single source. State the expected codes: SCOPE_PENDING_COUNSEL at token creation, A12's missing-scope refusal at call time, and FIL_PERSON_ONLY or MET_ATTEST_PERSON_ONLY only as a defence-in-depth check in the handler, tested with a principal of actor type AGNT or AGTU that carries the scope through a test-only override. Remove mark-audited from the list of token drafts and from the sensitive-agent-actions list.

findings.issue: Parts of the published sponsor_profile block have no governed source. The block carries performance lines incidents and complaints_resolved 'from audited tenant-scope values', but the closed metric vocabulary has no incidents or complaints key. A33's snapshot has complaints_open, not complaints_resolved. So these lines are always null, or a builder publishes them from some other source. trusts[] rows (planned vs actual yield, forecast vs actual growth, retained stake) have no metric keys and no rule that they must be audited, and they carry no basis or as_of. That leaves a hole in 'audited metrics only' and in G17's 'yields shown with basis and date'.
findings.fix: Add vehicle-scope and tenant-scope keys to the closed vocabulary: yield_planned_bps, yield_paid_bps, growth_forecast_bps, growth_actual_bps, retained_stake_bps, incidents_count and complaints_resolved_count. Name each source (A33 snapshot, A44, A48) and set its unit. State that every trusts[] figure is an audited metric_value carrying {value, unit, as_of, basis, metric_snapshot_id}, or null. Record with A33 or A44 where complaints_resolved comes from. Add a challenge in which a management trusts[] yield is nulled in the block.

findings.issue: Corrections that already-built ancestors must make are not scheduled before A45's build. A45 reads A33's distributions_on_time_pct and proof_of_property_score 'unchanged' as basis points, and it relies on A33's public 'Trusts on RealX' counting only publicly visible trusts. A33 (AM3, an ancestor) specifies neither. A43 (an ancestor) registers its G17 precheck on 'metrics.publish', an action id that will never exist. These appear only under 'Upstream corrections requested' at the Gate, and Specify's settled items (a)-(c) name only A03.1-A45. So the orchestrator will not run them first. ADM-29 and the published block can then be off by a factor of 100 or hold floats, the fidelity check on 'never 3' depends on A33's route, and A43's hook never fires.
findings.fix: Name follow-ups A33-fu-A45 (unit convention or _bp rename, a public count of visible trusts, a read of the about text and declared facts) and A43-fu-A45 (hook on M19.metricPublication.publish, drop GET /v1/metrics/public) as Specify-blocking items beside A03.1-A45. Alternatively, have A45 read A33's declared input unit and convert explicitly, with a unit test.

findings.issue: A76 asks for follow-up loop A45.1 (line 92): allowed_actions[] on every calendar, obligation, filing, grant, export, definition and publication row; and, on AML projection rows, A42's clock_policy, clock unit and remaining_ms. A45's spec has none of these, although it is being revised before any build. The projected rows expose days_remaining, which is the wrong unit for the 24-hour terrorism-financing SMR clock. A102 calls registerExportMinimiser, which the spec names but does not include in the index.ts export list.
findings.fix: Fold A45.1 into this spec now. Add allowed_actions[] (derived server-side from the caller's A03 cells, row state and person-only rules), and add clock_policy, clock_unit ('business_days' | 'hours') and remaining_ms on AML rows and on A45's own clocked rows. Add registerExportMinimiser to the index.ts exports. Add pass criteria for both. Otherwise, name A45.1-A76 and A45.1-A102 explicitly with their change lists.

findings.issue: The design contract for ADM-26 and ADM-29 conflicts with A51, the design-extension node that draws them. A51 line 191 draws the obligations table as Obligation / Regulator / Due / Owner / State. A51 line 194 draws ADM-29 with a Complaints column and 'On-time reporting percent'. A45 claims different column sets (Regime, Recipient, Evidence; 8 ADM-29 columns with complaints in the row detail), says A51 'draws them', and asks for no A51 correction beyond rows 141 and 143. A45's challenge includes 'a design-fidelity read ... against ADM-26's column sets', which has two conflicting references. The product map's ADM-26 mock also has an 'Object' column (Case 8812, PAD01, Platform, Q3), and regulatory_obligation has no field for it.
findings.fix: Pick one column set and record it in both specs. The simplest is to adopt A51's frame (Regulator rendered from regime), keep recipient, evidence_count and complaints as fields, and add an A51 correction for the ADM-29 Complaints column and the On-time label. Add object_ref and object_label to regulatory_obligation (subject such as a vehicle, licence, period or platform) so that the Object column has data.

findings.issue: The data-room challenge requires that 'A101 receives the sensitive read', but A101 depends on A45 and does not exist at A45's gate. As written, the challenge cannot be run.
findings.fix: At A45's gate, assert only that the audit event carries class sensitive, actor_type AGNT or AGTU and on_behalf_of. List the check that A101 receives the event as a named re-run at A101's gate.

findings.issue: The AML projection hides AML rows from every token, including the MLRO's and CCO's own agents. A42's token table lets those agents act on A42's reads and regulatory orders. So the calendar view differs between the person and the agent, and this D04 parity gap is not recorded as an exception for A100.
findings.fix: Either give MLRO and CCO tokens that hold A42's delegable AML read scope the projected rows, or record the gap in A100's exception list with its reason (tipping-off minimisation) and a counsel question.

findings.issue: The publication precheck refuses the whole publication for 'any sponsor figure or sponsor block whose tenant is suspended', and a block is built for every tenant with an active admission. One suspended sponsor can therefore block all platform figures and every other sponsor's block.
findings.fix: State that a suspended tenant gets no sponsor_profile block (A33 serves its status), that the precheck refuses only an explicit attempt to include one, and add a challenge in which a publication succeeds while one tenant is suspended.
